spec.title: Does high government debt kill growth? Reinhart and Rogoff said growth averages -0.1% above 90% debt
spec.statement: Reinhart and Rogoff (American Economic Review, 2010) reported that rich countries with public debt above 90 percent of GDP grew by -0.1 percent a year on average. The figure was widely cited in arguments for austerity. This re-runs the code Herndon, Ash and Pollin published, on the authors' own working spreadsheet, without the coding error, the excluded years or the unusual weighting they identified. It's the critics' code, not the authors'.

source.authors: C. M. Reinhart, K. S. Rogoff; re-analysis by T. Herndon, M. Ash, R. Pollin

artifact.entrypoint: sed -n '1,236p' RR.R | sed '/library(xlsx)/d;/write.xlsx2/d' > /tmp/rr.R && echo 'cat("above90", RR.correct.mean[["Above 90%"]], "\n")' >> /tmp/rr.R && Rscript --vanilla /tmp/rr.R > rerun_output.txt

metric.name: average yearly growth above 90% debt, in percent
